findings.what: The cell says that any line holding a marker-like comment is refused, and also «the lines between are never read». Read literally, the second skips the marker-like rule inside an open region. Plant (f) — block D's end marker on one line with the element before it — then gives «index.html: line 35: an opening marker while the order region of line 23 is open». F46, the sketch and PB-6 give «line 27: a marker that is not alone on its line or not one of the four forms», and PB-6 asserts the line and the rule. Measured on my tree with the designer's plants: the sketch (every line read) refuses P5 at line 27 with «not alone»; the copy that reads such a comment as text (M91) refuses it at line 35 with «an opening marker while …». Both readings fail closed. Only the asserted line and rule differ, so a developer who follows the literal words would turn PB-6 (f) red.
findings.needed: State in 4.11 that every line is read for the four forms and for a marker-like comment, inside a region as well. Only the content of the lines between a region's markers is not interpreted, because it is cut whole.
